scope: GF180 C/D and IHP standard single-finger NMOS/PMOS physical geometry points, native full DRC and strict LVS, seven physical faults per layout, and layout regeneration. Not complete device-family, continuous operating-range, antenna/density or foundry qualification.
changes: GF180 width 0.22 to 10 um and length 0.28 to 10 um; IHP width 0.15 to 10 um and length 0.13 to 10 um, on the existing 5 nm grid.
Flared source/drain contact landings enclose contacts without increasing channel width.
Body-tap shape identity remains stable when resizing across the contact-landing threshold; source, drain, gate and body pin identities survive save/reopen.

historical_candidates.note: Initial source, pilot/full runs, original test expectations and failed/aborted invocations are retained. The final body-tap regression fails on the initial candidate and passes after correcting shape-role order.

failures_preserved: Initial Linux invocation had two module/path setup errors and two simulator skips.
Corrected Linux invocation exposed six obsolete range subtest expectations; final tests reject values outside the newly tested generator bounds.
Initial sandboxed Windows run reported execution errors and was stopped. Both subsequent ordinary-account runs passed.
Body-tap identity regression fails against the initial candidate; the final source fixes it.
limits: Only six standard MOS catalog views in GF180 C/D and IHP; one finger and multiplicity one.
Seventy-two sampled published geometry points, not proof of every dimension combination on the supported grid.
Physical DRC/LVS runs use local Linux/WSL tools; Windows executes geometry, regeneration, serialization and simulator regressions.
Other device-family layouts, alternate models, full operating envelopes, statistical/RF coverage and installed-release acceptance remain open.
